purpose: Trace semantic ownership across upstream contracts, wiring, dataflow/AST ADT, manifest, graph, IR, CLI, SDK, React and example frontend; identify safe next integrations without inventing consumers.

checks.name: upstream operation identity contract is closed and authority-owned
operation identity runtime algebra preserves route evidence/provenance/reasoning
manifest builder validates and closes canonical AST before semantic model construction
manifest builder derives dataflow seeds from canonical source model
AST dataflow contract exposes read-only authority rather than execution solver
generic DataFlowInterface separates producer execution and consumer authority
IR projection uses canonical semantic dataflow authority
graph relation projection is a separate structural semantic lane
CLI emitter projects upstream operation identity capability rather than classifying HTTP method
SDK fails closed when operation identity or hook capability is absent
React intent wrapper consumes explicit domain intent capability
example frontend keeps Axios transport separate from semantic route identity

boundaryContractTrace.name: ProviderContainerOperations
boundaryContractTrace.wiring: provider AST canonical projection into CompleteLaravelSourceModel / manifest seeds
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: manifest/graph only if raw operations remain semantically distinct from ProviderContainerBindings
boundaryContractTrace.finding: Public type is not internally consumed; neighboring ProviderContainerBindings is already used as the canonical normalized container shape. Do not wire a second lane until providerAstCanonical proves a separate raw-operation stage is needed.
boundaryContractTrace.action: preserve; verify producer-level distinction before integrating

boundaryContractTrace.name: ControllerExpressionFact
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: semantic dataflow authority and IR projection
boundaryContractTrace.finding: The contract carries expression, origin, and source provenance; inspect producer output before mapping to existing ControllerSemanticVariableFlow to avoid duplicating provenance.
boundaryContractTrace.action: candidate for a producer-to-dataflow projection only if no equivalent fact is already emitted

boundaryContractTrace.name: ExpressionDefinition
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: AST judgments and dataflow seed construction
boundaryContractTrace.finding: The shape is already provenance-bearing; no new bridge should be added if expression AST output already includes the same expression and span.
boundaryContractTrace.action: preserve; compare producer shape and existing provenance before wiring

boundaryContractTrace.name: RequestRouteParameterName
boundaryContractTrace.producer: route parameter extraction and request binding
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: manifest and generated SDK route parameter reference
boundaryContractTrace.finding: Keep request-side identity distinct from transport path strings; do not reconstruct route parameter meaning in SDK/React.
boundaryContractTrace.action: trace exact source producer; only adapt at upstream boundary

boundaryContractTrace.name: RequestUriValue
boundaryContractTrace.wiring: request context facts to semantic model
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: request analysis only when URI semantics are needed
boundaryContractTrace.finding: Potential overlap with RouteIdentity/RoutePath; URI runtime context and declared route identity are not automatically equivalent.
boundaryContractTrace.action: preserve until a consumer proves the URI-context capability is needed

boundaryContractTrace.name: RequestIpAddress
boundaryContractTrace.wiring: request context facts to semantic model
boundaryContractTrace.finding: No reason to add this to route identity or generic dataflow by default; it is request context, not route classification.
boundaryContractTrace.action: preserve as optional vocabulary; add a producer only when source evidence/consumer exists

boundaryContractTrace.name: ValidationRuleDefinition
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: schema/Zod projection, not a frontend semantic classifier
boundaryContractTrace.finding: Validation definitions should lower once at the upstream semantic boundary; Zod is a target projection and must not infer Laravel rule intent independently.
boundaryContractTrace.action: compare with ValidationRule and RequestValidationCapability; share canonical evidence if equivalent

boundaryContractTrace.name: SchemaRelationTarget
boundaryContractTrace.finding: Table-model pair belongs to schema relation semantics; graph should consume projected relation, not rediscover table/model links.
boundaryContractTrace.action: wire only if the schema relation authority does not already emit the equivalent target

boundaryContractTrace.name: CanonicalSourceNode
boundaryContractTrace.consumer: generic source-boundary operations and AST/dataflow adapters
boundaryContractTrace.finding: CanonicalSourceNode and SourceBoundaryInput describe overlapping views of the same source kinds; converting one to the other without a consumer adds an extra classification pass.
boundaryContractTrace.action: keep type-only until a shared boundary consumer needs the closed tagged form

boundaryContractTrace.name: SourceBoundaryInput
boundaryContractTrace.finding: Its discriminants are a useful closed ADT but no consumer should be invented just to remove zero-reference status.
boundaryContractTrace.action: candidate for source visitor algebra only when it replaces duplicated switches/classifiers

architecture.owns: source evidence, source spans, closed AST/ADT, framework-specific semantic facts
semantic interpretation, capability identity, proof/provenance, closed judgment
validated conversion of canonical AST/source model into manifest seeds, dataflow input and structural relations; no new classification
generic execution upstream; downstream receives read-only authority, closure and stable identity
structural relation projection only; does not replace semantic dataflow
projection and execution from explicit upstream capabilities; no Laravel semantic reclassification

nonGoals: Do not delete or empty public types solely because internal symbol usage is zero.
Do not add fake consumers to make public contracts appear used.
Do not route request URI/IP context into route identity without a domain-level equivalence proof.
Do not introduce a second AST conversion if CompleteSourceAst already carries the same canonical node and provenance.
Do not claim a TypeScript 7 build from an audit run on another TypeScript compiler version.
validationLimits: This is a contract/path audit, not a full runtime or end-to-end test.
TypeScript 7 compatibility is not established by this audit; compiler API audit compatibility must be verified with the repository-pinned TS 7 toolchain.
The 10 zero-reference declarations are preserved; recommendations are trace decisions, not proof that public contracts are dead.
